story.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Create a professional hand-drawn 2D FULL-BODY cel-animation sprite sheet of the EXACT attached approved apricot puppy. This image is the character identity reference, NOT a fixed pose constraint. Preserve the same large rounded head proportion, cream forehead blaze/muzzle/chest/paws/tail tip, golden apricot fur, brown floppy ears, brown eyes and nose, sage green collar with a SINGLE round brass tag, same elegant dark brown outlines and soft shading. Never redesign the puppy. Dog anatomy, FOUR legs, canine paws, no human hands.
OUTPUT: EXACTLY EIGHT columns by EIGHT rows =64 equally sized square cells, chronological left-to-right then next row. Transparent background, no lines, no lettering, no shadows outside puppy, no repeated ghost poses. High resolution 4096x4096 if possible. All cells have constant camera scale (same head size) and ground baseline at90% cell height; whole dog and little prop fit, with generous 8% margin; no cropping. Three-quarter side facing RIGHT throughout. Smoothly changing adjacent drawings with small changes, true complete character frames, NO abrupt pose changes or random unrelated actions.
ACTION is one charming purposeful 'working on a task' story, animated with clear weight, anticipation and follow-through:
Frames1-8: starts in EXACT approved seated neutral posture, notices a tiny sage paper task scroll on ground just ahead of paws, looks down then gradually leans chest forward and extends hind legs to stand on all four. Frames9-16: fully standing, slowly lowers head to sniff the scroll, closes canine mouth around center of it then lifts head holding it. Frames17-24: carries scroll in mouth, takes TWO SHORT natural alternating steps toward right, visible four-leg gait and gentle head/ear followthrough; remains inside cell. Frames25-32: stops, lowers hindquarters and chest, flexes elbows into natural puppy lying-down sphinx posture, brings scroll to ground between both forepaws. Frames33-40: lying down, alternates pressing the scroll with nearer/farther forepaw, investigates it with nose, small purposeful chew or nudge. Frames41-48: stays lying, lifts head to glance happily toward viewer with small smile and tail wag, then returns attention to scroll. Frames49-56: finishes inspection, releases scroll on ground, slowly pushes forelegs up and tucks hindquarters back into sitting. Frames57-64: sitting settles gently into EXACT original neutral seated pose and original placement, tail settles; tiny scroll stays on ground ahead, no disappearing objects. First and last puppy pose must match identity reference closely. Every frame must be a useful IN-BETWEEN, especially sitting-to-standing and standing-to-lying and lying-to-sitting. No skeleton look, no floating, no teleporting, no melting anatomy, no disembodied limbs. This must feel like a real cute puppy performing one connected action, not 64 unrelated puppy illustrations. Do not make a diagram or a contact sheet of only major keyposes. Prioritize smooth incremental movement and exact identity continuity.

lower.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset: sixteen consecutive complete cel-animation in-between drawings of the EXACT puppy in the attached images.
